sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Open WebUI is a self-hosted, ChatGPT-style web interface for AI models. It connects to local models through Ollama or to any OpenAI-compatible API, and it is built to run entirely offline if you want.
sixtySeconds.problem: Local models usually come with only a command line, and cloud chat apps keep your conversations on someone else's servers. Open WebUI gives you a polished chat interface you host yourself, for local and cloud models alike.
whoFor: Ollama users who want a web chat interface
Teams hosting a private AI chat
Developers comparing local and cloud models
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for the most popular self-hosted chat UI for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible models. Its license requires keeping the Open WebUI branding.
requirements: Docker, or Python 3.12 with pip or uv

overview: Open WebUI runs as a web app you open in your browser. Point it at Ollama for local models, or give it an OpenAI API key or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint for cloud and local models.

Docker images come in several flavours: main with local AI dependencies, slim using external services for embeddings and documents, cuda for NVIDIA acceleration, ollama with Ollama bundled, and dev. Options like OLLAMA_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY and HF_HUB_OFFLINE configure it.

There's also a native desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux, and ecosystem projects for agent terminals and knowledge base sync. Code is under the Open WebUI License, which requires preserving the branding.

steps.title: Start the container
steps.body: Add -e OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://your-ollama-server:11434 to connect to Ollama on another server.
steps.code: docker run -d -p 3000:8080 --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway -v open-webui:/app/backend/data --name open-webui --restart always ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
